rows.label: Concept
rows.text: When light in a denser medium meets a rarer boundary, the refracted ray bends away; at the **critical angle** C it grazes the surface ($\sin C = 1/n$), and beyond C the light is **totally internally reflected** — returned completely into the denser medium. Two conditions: travel **denser → rarer** and **i > C** (NEB 2022, 2024, 2m).…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: - sin C = 1/n = n₂/n₁ - Glass-air: C ≈ 41.8°; diamond: C ≈ 24.4°

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **Denser → rarer only:** light going from air into glass can never totally internally reflect.  ·  **sin C = 1/n** — the critical angle shrinks as the refractive index grows.

rows.text: ***Diamond*** — C = 24.4° traps light, creating brilliance.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: **The critical angle is where refraction dies** — sin C = 1/n comes straight from Snell's law with r = 90°.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Conditions: denser→rarer; i > C. sin C = 1/n.  ·  TIR is lossless — better than any silvered mirror.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Fibre-optic cables carry internet traffic by total internal reflection across thousands of kilometres of glass.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — Light Trapped Inside Past a certain angle, light hitting the inside of a glass–air boundary doesn't escape at all — it reflects perfectly, better than any mirror. Total internal reflection powers optical fibres, the glitter of diamonds and the prisms in binoculars.  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts (NEB 2021, 2022, 2024) ### 2.1 From refraction to total reflection As the angle of incidence i (in the denser medium) grows, the angle of refraction r grows faster. At the **critical angle** C, the refracted ray grazes along the surface (r = 90°). Beyond C there is no refracted ray — the light is completely returned: **total internal reflection**.…  ·  ## 3. Conceptual Relationships - **To Topic 70/71:** the critical angle is Snell's law with r = 90°. - **To Topic 72:** a slab beyond C becomes a mirror — the basis of light guides. - **To modern physics:** fibre-optic TIR carries the internet across oceans.
